verdict.line: You lose level 1-5 trades where Sion lands Q (Cryptic Gaze) into Enrage-boosted autos, but you win from level 6 onward once R (Fury of the Sands) and stacked Q (Siphoning Strike) take over, matching the 54.2% win rate over 153 games.

brief.thesis: Sion's only hard punish tool is Q (Cryptic Gaze), a 550-range single-target stun on a 12/11/10/9/8s cooldown, backed by Enrage trading HP for AD; he has no dash, no second CC, and nothing to stop a scaling stack-and-survive plan. Nasus just has to not get stunned-and-chained before level 6, farm Q stacks and Soul Eater lifesteal through the poke, then let Fury of the Sands flip the lane the moment it's up, which is exactly what the 153-game head-to-head rewards.

theirWindow.when: Q up, you're overextended past minions
theirWindow.what: Sion can stun you from 550 range then free-swing with Enrage active, burning his own HP for AD to shred yours fast; stay behind your wave so the stun can't chain into a kill.

yourWindow.when: His Q down, post-level 6 with R up
yourWindow.what: Without Cryptic Gaze he has no engage or peel, so walk up and land Siphoning Strike (Q) freely; threaten Fury of the Sands (R) to force him off farm, since his only answer is popping Death's Caress (W) early and eating the trade anyway.

start.why: Taken in 66.9% of games (56.9% win rate over 123) because the flat damage reduction on the first attack from a unit each few seconds blunts both Sion's poke autos and his Enrage-boosted trades.

boots.why: Picked 59.8% of the time (48.6% win rate over 107 games); the cooldown reduction tightens your Q-W-E loop so you're stacking Siphoning Strike and threatening Wither more often per minute.

core.why: First item in the highest-sample core path (51.5% win rate over 33 games); the damage and tempo let you punish Sion whenever his Q is down.
Caps Sion's attack speed from Cannibalism and Enrage auto-resets, directly countering his all-in pattern.
Stacks with Soul Eater's lifesteal to win extended trades and outlast his HP-burning Enrage.

runes.keystoneWhy: The sustain and move speed from auto-attacking minions lets you heal through Sion's poke and Enrage trades while farming Q stacks, and gives you the speed to disengage after a Cryptic Gaze stun.

summoners.why: The highest-pick, highest-win combo (47.9% pick, 52.7% win rate); Teleport lets you reset waves and keep stacking Q without losing tempo, while Ghost closes distance or escapes since Nasus has no dash to answer a Cryptic Gaze stun chain.

playing.title: Farm every Q stack safely
playing.detail: Prioritize landing Siphoning Strike on cannon and melee minions whenever it's safe; Soul Eater lifesteal keeps you topped off against Sion's poke, and every stack scales your level 6+ trades.

playing.title: Respect Cryptic Gaze range
playing.detail: Stay outside 550 range or behind minions whenever Sion's Q is off cooldown; getting stunned into his Enrage-boosted autos is the main way you lose HP before you can fight back.

playing.title: Don't swing into a live shield
playing.detail: Death's Caress (W, 8s cooldown) absorbs damage and explodes on expiry or reactivation; don't dump your full Q rotation into it, wait it out or burn it early with Spirit Fire pressure.

playing.title: Flip the lane with Fury of the Sands
playing.detail: From level 6, use R's 120s window to engage: the health, range, and max-health-drain bonuses swing fights in your favor, matching the pattern of regaining lane control post-6.

playing.title: Drop Spirit Fire before committing
playing.detail: E, on a 12s cooldown at 650 range, reduces armor in its zone; place it under Sion before trading to multiply your Q and auto damage.

playing.title: Hold Wither for his escape
playing.detail: Save W (15/14/13/12/11s cooldown, 700 range) to slow Sion's movement and attack speed once his Enrage is spent and he tries to walk away from a losing trade.

playing.title: Play the stats, not the panic
playing.detail: Despite his early stun pressure, the 153-game head-to-head sits at 54.2% in your favor; don't force all-ins at level 1-2, just survive to stack and let R carry you mid-lane.

brief.patchCaveat: Build paths, runes, summoner spells, and win rates are pulled from measured Nasus vs Sion games on the current patch via OP.GG; the ability timings and trade-window reading are our own tactical analysis.

stats.opponentTip: Be careful of Sion’s (Q) and ranged abilities used inside brushes. Farm and heal with [Q] to gain stacks, while looking for an opportunity post-level 6 by using [R] to slowly regain lane control.
